documents.unit: Office of the AVP for Academic Affairs and Center for Academic Technology
documents.title: AI Syllabus Statements
documents.stance_why: The memo says "there is not a one-size-fits-all approach" and offers three syllabus statements (prohibit, limited, broad) that faculty "are not required to use", so the university sets no stance itself and hands the choice to instructors with tiers.
tiers: Prohibit all use of AI tools
documents.summary: A short memo from the AVP for Academic Affairs and the Center for Academic Technology giving faculty three optional syllabus statements for AI writing tools: full prohibition, limited use as announced by the instructor, and broad use with citation. Each ties violations to the academic misconduct policy.

units.why: The memo says "we encourage you to consider including a statement governing the use of these tools", asking instructors to put AI expectations in syllabi. It is a recommendation, not a mandate, so P09 fits partly (modality should).
units.anchor: we encourage you to consider including a statement governing the use of these tools
units.fit_note: Syllabus statement is encouraged, not required.

units.why: "there is not a one-size-fits-all approach" explains why the memo offers several statements that "vary according to the type of use", so it names categories of AI use. That is P05, not P04, because the memo defines three named options.
units.anchor: we have crafted three separate syllabus statements that vary according to the type of use

units.why: "you are not required to use the provided statements" leaves the choice of statement and policy to each instructor, so the unit hands the decision down (P04).
units.anchor: you are not required to use the provided statements

units.why: "not permitted for any stage or phase of work in this class" is a full ban on AI writing tools in the course, so P01 (default prohibition) and unit_stance prohibit.
units.anchor: are not permitted for any stage or phase of work in this class

units.why: "will be considered a violation of the University's academic misconduct policy" classifies prohibited use as misconduct handled by disciplinary procedures, so P36.
units.anchor: your actions will be considered a violation of the University’s academic misconduct policy

units.why: "there may be opportunities to make use of AI writing tools" and "You will be informed as to when, where, and how" make permission case-by-case, set by the instructor per activity (P04).
units.anchor: You will be informed as to when, where, and how these tools are permitted

units.why: "along with guidance for attribution" says permitted uses come with attribution instructions, i.e. AI use is to be acknowledged; nearest type P24, but the detail is left to the instructor.
units.frag_start: You will be informed as to when,
units.fit_note: Attribution method is not specified; instructor will give guidance.

units.why: "Any use outside of this permission will be considered a violation" makes unpermitted use misconduct, which is also a default-restrictive rule; classified as P36 because its enforcement language is the load-bearing part.
units.anchor: Any use outside of this permission will be considered a violation of the University’s

units.why: "are welcome in this class" states a permissive default for AI writing tools, so P02 and unit_stance permit.
units.anchor: AI writing tools (such as ChatGPT) are welcome in this class

units.why: "provided that you properly cite when and how you use the tool" makes citing AI use a condition of permission, so P24 (disclose with submission).
units.anchor: provided that you properly cite when and how you use the tool

units.why: "Using an AI tool to generate content without proper attribution qualifies as a violation" makes nondisclosure itself the violation, which is P28 (rather than P36, because the rule is about attribution failure).
units.anchor: Using an AI tool to generate content without proper attribution qualifies as a violation

notes: Single short memo; all units coded. Course layer deferred in collect file.
